title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Marina Lopez
summary: Consolidated engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure patterns, model-serving requirements, observability SLOs, and performance targets. Includes ADR index for major architecture decisions.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical standards across API design, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It is intended for engineers, architects, and product managers to provide a single reference for daily design and implementation decisions and to record architectural decisions (ADRs).

Scope

- API standards (REST/HTTP, contract stability, versioning, error handling, pagination, rate limiting)
- Coding standards (language-specific conventions, testing, linting, package structure)
- Infrastructure standards (cloud accounts, networking, IaC patterns, secrets, capacity planning)
- Model-serving standards (model packaging, quantization profiles, rollout / canary policy, fallback strategies)
- Observability standards (metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, on-call alerts)
- Performance standards (latency P95, throughput expectations, batching guidelines, cost controls)
- Decision records (ADRs) index and guidance for creating new ADRs

Principles

1. Production-first: favor predictable SLOs, observability, and automated rollbacks over experimental shortcuts.
2. Developer ergonomics: APIs and infra should be easy to use, secure-by-default, and well documented.
3. Cost-awareness: prefer designs that make unit economics visible and controllable.
4. Compatibility: deprecate gracefully; maintain clear compatibility guarantees for public contracts.
5. Incremental change: prefer small, reversible changes with canaries and feature flags.

API Standards

- Protocols and Formats
  - Primary public endpoints: HTTPS/REST with JSON Schema-based contracts. gRPC internal-only where high-throughput/low-latency is required.
  - All APIs must publish a JSON Schema (or OpenAPI) contract stored in the api-contracts repo and surfaced in the API catalog.

- Versioning and Compatibility
  - Use semantic versioning for major API surfaces. Breaking changes require an ADR and a 90-day migration period plus compatibility shims where feasible.
  - Path-based versioning: /v1/, /v2/ for externally-consumed endpoints.

- Error Handling
  - Return structured error objects: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional}. Map to standard HTTP status codes.
  - Transient server errors (5xx) must include retry-after header when appropriate.

- Rate Limiting and Quotas
  - Standard headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
  - Graceful enforcement: soft limit warnings (429 with metadata) for hosted endpoints, strict enforcement for dedicated/private deployments per contract.

- Pagination and Sorting
  - Cursor-based pagination for large result sets; default page size 50, max 1000 for admin APIs.

Coding Standards

- Languages and Tooling
  - Primary languages: Go (services), Python (infra & evals), TypeScript (frontend & SDKs).
  - Use repo-specific linters and fixed formatting (gofmt, black, prettier).

- Testing
  - Unit coverage minimum: 60% for backend business logic modules.
  - Integration tests required for any changes touching model-serving, routing, or billing flows. Use CI test matrices to run heavy integration suites on PRs and full test runs on main.

- PRs and Reviews
  - All production changes require at least one approver from the owning team and one from the platform or security team for infra-impacting changes.
  - Use feature flags for behavioral changes; include rollout plan in PR description.

Infrastructure Standards

- Infrastructure as Code
  - All infra changes go through Terraform modules located in infra-terraform. Modules must include input/output docs and example usages.
  - State management: centralized Terraform Cloud/Enterprise workspaces per account.

- Networking and Security
  - Default deny VPCs with explicit service egress rules. Use VPC endpoints for S3-like object stores.
  - KMS-backed secrets for all production secrets; never commit plaintext credentials.

- Capacity and Autoscaling
  - Dedicated GPU pools should have target utilization 60-80% on normal load. Autoscaling policies must include cooldowns and max burst caps.
  - Capacity plans must be reviewed quarterly by SRE and Product.

Model-Serving Standards

- Model Packaging and Versions
  - Models are artifacts with immutable version IDs. Each version includes: model-config.yaml, weights (signed), quantization profile, and eval bundle.
  - Model metadata must include expected sequence length, memory footprint, supported batch sizes, and recommended kernel variants.

- Quantization and Profiles
  - Quantization profiles stored in /quantization-profiles with expected accuracy deltas measured on canonical eval sets. Profiles: fp16, int8, int8-fp32-hybrid.

- Rollouts and Fallbacks
  - Canary policy: 1% traffic for 24 hours, 10% for 48 hours, then progressive rollout if no regressions. Automated rollback if error rate > 3x baseline or latency P95 increases by > 40%.
  - Fallbacks: define a compatible model variant and/or lower-cost endpoint for graceful degradation.

- Observability and Cost Controls
  - Each model version must emit per-request token counts, per-token latency histograms, and predicted cost estimates.

Observability Standards

- Metrics (Prometheus native)
  - Required metrics: request_count, request_errors, request_latency_seconds{quantile}, tokens_generated_total, batch_size_dist.
  - Naming convention: <service>_<resource>_<metric> (snake_case).

- Tracing
  - Use OpenTelemetry for traces. Trace IDs must be propagated through request routing, batching layers, and downstream model inference components.

- Logging
  - Structured JSON logs with stable keys: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, user_id (if applicable), message. Avoid logging PII.

- Dashboards and Alerts
  - Standard dashboards: per-service health (QPS, errors, P95/P99 latency), cost-per-token breakdown, model-regression dashboard (quality metrics vs. baseline).
  - Alerting thresholds (example):
    - Error rate: page at service-level if error_rate_5m > 1% AND request_count_5m > 1000
    - Latency: page if P95 > target_latency * 2 for 10 minutes
    - SLO burn: page when error budget < 10% remaining.

Performance Standards

- Latency SLOs (example guide)
  - Hosted API text-generation: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms for small models (<= 1B effective params), P95 < 700ms for mid models (1-10B), and defined per-model in model-catalog.
  - Embedding endpoints: P95 < 200ms.

- Throughput and Batching
  - Batching should be workload-aware; target average batch sizes documented per endpoint. Use adaptive batching in runtime with max batch size constraints per model.

- Cost Targets
  - Track tokens-per-dollar at service and model level. Quarterly reviews to flag models > 2x median cost for category.

ADRs (Decision Records)

- ADR Process
  1. Create a short ADR (title, status, context, decision, consequences, alternatives) in the adr/ directory.
  2. Link ADR to PR that implements the change and reference related dashboards/alerts.
  3. Reviewers: architecture owners + impacted service owners.
  4. Publish ADR and update this document if it affects standards.

- ADR Index (selected recent decisions)
  - ADR-2025-11: "Adopt JSON Schema + OpenAPI for public API contracts" - decision: JSON Schema + OpenAPI tooling for validation and mock generation.
  - ADR-2026-02: "Standardize model artifact metadata format" - decision: model-config.yaml with standardized keys for memory, latency, batch sizes.
  - ADR-2026-06: "Use OpenTelemetry as tracing standard" - decision: adopt OpenTelemetry as vendor-neutral tracing format.

Governance and Ownership

- Ownership model
  - Standards maintained by Architecture Guild (rotating chairs from eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, eng-infra). Changes to standards require at least two approvers: Architecture Guild and owning team.

- Review cadence
  - Major standards reviewed quarterly. Critical infra or security changes will trigger ad-hoc reviews.

Appendix: Example snippets

- Example error schema (JSON Schema snippet)
  {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["code", "message"],
    "properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}, "message": {"type": "string"}, "details": {"type": "object"}}
  }

- Example Terraform module header (doc table)
  | Field | Description | Example |
  |------|-------------|---------|
  | name | module name | gke-cluster |
  | env  | environment | prod |
